newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cyprus EU membership could defuse tension - Council.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus EU membership could defuse tension - Council.

text.p: The Council of Europe said on Wednesday that letting Cyprus join the European Union could help resolve tensions over the island.

"Membership of the EU will entail significant economic and political advantages for the two communities. It will be a major factor of stability," the Council's parliamentary assembly said in a resolution.

Cyprus, which hopes to start EU accession talks next year, has been divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded and occupied the northern third of the island after a Greek Cypriot coup engineered by Greece's then ruling military junta.

"The resolution clearly means that Cyprus can become a member of the EU, even if no definite solution has been found to the partition problem," Doros Christodoulides, the island's representative to the assembly told Reuters.
But Turkish deputy Ismail Cem told a news conference: "If Cyprus's membership of the EU became established, the island's division would probably become permanent."
